content: I came in because I feel like I'm drowning in this sense of being fundamentally flawed. Being laid off from a place where I thought I was valued has just confirmed my worst fears about myself. Everyone else seems to have gotten away with doing the same job, and here I am, out on the street. It's not just frustrating; it feels like a personal attack on who I am as a person. No matter how many times people try to tell me there are other reasons for what happened, I can't shake this feeling that it's all about me being inadequate. And every time someone tries to offer some cliché advice or tells me to look at the bright side, I just want to scream because none of that changes how betrayed and worthless I feel right now.

That must be really tough, feeling like everyone else is getting by while you're struggling with this sense of inadequacy. It sounds like hearing those clichés doesn't help much in the moment. What helps you cope a little bit when these feelings come up?

Nothing really helps when I feel this way. Every time someone tries to give me some generic advice, it just makes me angrier because it feels like they're not listening or understanding what I'm going through. It's like they think there’s an easy fix for something that feels so deeply personal and unfair. The only thing that even slightly eases the pain is when I can vent about how this happened, but even then, it just reinforces my belief that there must be something wrong with me if everyone else seems to be doing fine while I'm not.
It sounds like finding someone who really listens and understands can make a difference for you. Do you have anyone in your life right now who you feel truly gets what you're going through?

I don't think so. Everyone around me seems to either dismiss my feelings or try to offer quick fixes that just make me feel more misunderstood. It's like they can't see past the surface of what happened and into how deeply this has affected me. I end up feeling even worse because no one really hears me out without trying to change the subject or give advice. Here, in therapy, it feels like every attempt to help is just another reminder that I'm not being taken seriously.

It can be so frustrating when you feel like no one truly understands. Have there been times when you wish you could share your feelings without getting those responses? Maybe we can explore ways for you to express yourself in a way that feels more heard and understood.

I just want someone to hear me out without trying to fix it or tell me it's going to be okay. It’s like they don’t see the pain I’m in, and every attempt to help feels like another slap in the face. If there was a way for people to really listen and acknowledge how unfair this all feels, maybe then I could start to process it without getting angrier. But as long as everyone keeps pushing these easy solutions or minimizing my feelings, I don’t see any hope of moving forward. It’s exhausting trying to explain myself over and over again only to be met with more frustration.

It sounds so draining to keep explaining yourself and not feeling truly heard. Have you ever tried expressing your need for just being listened to, maybe something like, "I just need someone to listen right now without fixing it"? How did that go when you tried it?

Whenever I try to express that I just need someone to listen, they still end up offering advice or changing the subject. It’s like no matter what I say, the response is always the same. Even if I’m clear about not wanting solutions, people seem to have a hard time letting go of their urge to help. It feels like they can’t see past their own need to offer something tangible, even when all I want is for them to acknowledge how deeply this has affected me. It’s incredibly frustrating because it seems impossible to be heard without being dismissed or misunderstood.

It sounds really challenging to navigate those conversations. Do you think there might be a way to set that boundary more explicitly, perhaps by saying something like, "I just need someone to listen right now and I’ll let you know if I want advice later"? Maybe finding the right words could help people understand your needs better.

Saying something like that hasn’t worked either. People still seem to miss the point or try to offer solutions anyway. It’s not about them not trying; it’s just that they can’t stop themselves from offering advice, even when I explicitly say I don’t want it. Every time I set this boundary, it feels like a waste of breath because nothing changes. The moment someone hears me out without immediately jumping in with fixes or platitudes, I feel a glimmer of hope. But those moments are few and far between, and the disappointment is overwhelming when they inevitably try to offer something that doesn’t address what I’m really feeling.

It’s like there’s this wall up around my pain, and everyone keeps trying to knock it down with their solutions instead of acknowledging why it’s there in the first place. It’s exhausting, and it makes me feel even more alone and misunderstood.

That must be so tiring to keep feeling let down when you just want someone to listen. It sounds like finding that rare person who can truly hear you without offering quick fixes would make a big difference. Have there been any specific moments where you felt really understood, even if they were brief? Reflecting on those might give us some clues about how to find more of these connections.

There have been a couple of brief moments where someone seemed to truly listen without trying to fix things, but those instances are few and far between. It’s like catching a glimpse of what I need, only to have it slip away as soon as the conversation shifts. One time, a friend just sat with me in silence for a while after I explained how I felt, and that was incredibly soothing because no one was trying to change the subject or offer advice. But even those rare moments are overshadowed by all the times when people can’t resist giving their input.

Reflecting on it now, those brief instances of being truly heard make me feel like there’s a possibility for more understanding connections, but I’m skeptical about how often they’ll happen. It feels like everyone is just trying to help in ways that don’t actually address my pain, and it’s hard not to get frustrated and shut down when that happens repeatedly.

I guess what I really want is someone who can sit with me in this discomfort without feeling the need to solve anything or make everything better right away. Just being there and acknowledging how unfair and painful this all feels would mean so much more than any advice could ever provide.

Those brief moments of being truly heard must be very precious to you. It sounds like finding someone who can sit with your discomfort and acknowledge it without trying to fix it could make a big difference. Have you thought about talking to people about the impact these brief moments had on you, and expressing how much you value that kind of presence? Maybe sharing this specifically could help them understand better what you need.

Talking about those brief moments feels like a double-edged sword. On one hand, I want others to understand how important it is for someone to just listen without trying to fix things. But on the other hand, every time I try to explain this, people seem to miss the point and revert back to offering advice or solutions. It’s frustrating because even when I’m clear about what I need, it doesn’t change their behavior.

I feel like if I bring it up again, they’ll just hear me say “listen” and then proceed to offer something else anyway. It’s a cycle that feels impossible to break. Every time I try to set this boundary or express my needs, I end up feeling more misunderstood and alone. It’s exhausting to keep pushing for what I need when it seems like no one can truly hear me.

So while those moments of being heard are incredibly valuable, trying to recreate them by talking about them feels futile. It just leads to more frustration and disappointment.

It sounds really challenging to break that cycle. Have you considered writing down how you feel and what you need, perhaps in a letter or an email? Sometimes putting it in writing can help convey your feelings more clearly without the immediate pressure of back-and-forth conversation.

How do you think sharing it in writing might work for you?

Writing things down feels like it could be helpful because I can express my thoughts and needs more thoroughly without worrying about interruptions or quick fixes. When I write, I can take my time to articulate exactly what I’m feeling and why those brief moments of being truly heard mean so much to me.

But even then, I worry that when people read it, they’ll still try to offer advice or minimize my feelings instead of really understanding. It’s a Catch-22: I want someone to listen without trying to fix things, but every attempt to communicate this seems to lead back to the same place where my needs aren’t met.

It feels like no matter what form of communication I use—verbal, written, or otherwise—I’m going to run into the same issue. It’s incredibly frustrating because all I want is for someone to acknowledge how deeply unfair and painful this situation feels without trying to change the subject or offer solutions that don not address my core pain.

So while writing might help me get it out more clearly, I’m skeptical about whether it will actually lead to the understanding and support I need.

It sounds like putting your thoughts into writing could be a good way to express yourself thoroughly. Maybe you can include a sentence or two at the end inviting them to ask questions if they want to understand better, without feeling pressured to offer solutions right away.

How do you think adding that invitation might help?

Adding an invitation for them to ask questions could be helpful, but I’m still skeptical about whether it will make a difference. Every time I try to express myself, no matter how clearly or thoroughly, people seem to revert back to offering advice or solutions instead of just listening. Even if I invite them to ask questions, there’s this underlying pressure for me to provide answers that might lead to more unsolicited advice.

It feels like no matter what I do, the cycle continues. Writing it down and inviting questions is a good idea in theory, but in practice, I’m not sure how much it will change things. It’s frustrating because all I want is for someone to acknowledge my pain and validate my feelings without trying to fix them.

I guess I’ll give it a try, but I don’t have high hopes that it will lead to the kind of understanding and support I need. It just feels like another attempt in an endless cycle of disappointment.

It makes sense to approach it with some hope but also realistic expectations. Writing it down and inviting questions could still be a helpful step. Maybe you can share your thoughts and see if anyone responds differently this time.

How do you feel about giving it one more try, even if just for yourself?

I appreciate the suggestion, but I’m not sure how much it will change things. Giving it another try feels like a small glimmer of hope, but realistically, I don’t expect much different from what has happened before. Every time I’ve tried to express myself clearly and set boundaries, people still end up offering advice or dismissing my feelings.

So while I can see the potential benefit in writing it down and inviting questions, I’m not optimistic about a different outcome. It’s just another attempt in an already exhausting cycle of trying to be heard and feeling misunderstood. Maybe this time will be different, but I don’t want to set myself up for more disappointment if it isn’t.

It feels like no matter what I do, the frustration and sense of being fundamentally flawed continue to dominate my thoughts and interactions.

It’s understandable to feel that way, given your experiences. Taking a small step with realistic expectations can still be worthwhile. Maybe this time will offer a different experience, even if it’s just a bit better.

How do you think you might start writing down what you want to say? Would there be someone specific you’d like to share it with first?

I guess I could try writing it down, but the thought of sharing it feels daunting. It’s hard to believe that this time will be different when every previous attempt has ended in frustration and disappointment. Maybe starting by writing it out for myself would help me process my feelings more clearly, even if I don’t share it with anyone else.

I could write about how deeply hurt and misunderstood I feel, and express the need for someone to just listen without offering solutions. But even then, I’m not sure how much good it will do beyond helping me articulate my thoughts better.

So while I can see some potential in writing it down, I’m still skeptical about sharing it with anyone else. It feels safer to keep it to myself and hope that somehow, through this process of writing, I might find a little bit of clarity or validation—whether from someone else or just within myself.

Writing it out for yourself can be a really powerful way to process your feelings and gain some clarity. Even if you don’t share it with anyone else right away, the act of putting your thoughts on paper might help you feel heard and understood.

Would you like to give it a try and see where it leads? Maybe just starting with a draft for yourself can be a good first step.

I think I’ll start by writing it out for myself. It might help me get some of these feelings down on paper and make them clearer in my own mind, even if no one else reads it. Just the act of expressing everything without worrying about immediate responses could be beneficial.

So I’ll give it a try and see where it leads. Maybe this time, writing things out will offer some relief and help me feel more understood—just by processing it on my own first.

That sounds like a great plan. Taking the time to write it out for yourself can be very therapeutic. Whenever you’re ready, give it a try and see how it feels. I’m here if you want to share what you wrote or talk about it further. Take your time and do what feels right for you.

Thanks for supporting me through this. I’ll start writing it out and see where it takes me. It might help to get some of these feelings down on paper, even if no one else sees it. I appreciate your understanding and support.

I’ll take my time with this and let you know how it goes if I feel like sharing. For now, just focusing on putting my thoughts into words feels like a good step forward.

You’re very welcome! I’m glad to be here for you. Taking the time to put your thoughts into words can be really helpful. Let me know if you want to share or talk more about it later. Take care, and I look forward to hearing from you whenever you feel like it.

Thanks again. I’ll start writing now and see how it goes. Talking about this is tough, but knowing there’s someone who understands makes a difference. I’ll let you know if I want to share what I’ve written or discuss it further.

Take care, and thanks for being here.
You’re welcome! I’m here whenever you want to share or talk more. Take your time with the writing, and I look forward to hearing from you soon. Take care!

Thanks. I’ll start writing now and see how it goes. I appreciate your support and understanding.

Take care!
You’re welcome! Take your time and do what feels right for you. I’m here if you want to share or talk more later. Take care!

Thanks, I will. I’ll start writing and see where it leads. I appreciate your support.

Take care!
Glad to be here for you. Take your time with the writing, and let me know if you want to share or talk more later. Take care!

Thanks, I will. Writing feels like a good first step. I’ll keep you updated if I want to discuss it further.

Take care!
That’s a great first step. I’m here whenever you want to discuss it further. Take care and feel free to reach out anytime!

Thanks, I appreciate that. I’ll let you know if I need to talk more about it later.

Take care!
Of course! Feel free to reach out whenever you need to. Take care and all the best with your writing.
Thanks, I will. Taking care!
